content:
alex_hernandez: Heads-up — after the runtime change merged yesterday I'm seeing a +18% bump in p95 TTFT on the small-chat suite when sampling is enabled. Can someone run a quick smoke bench and confirm it's not a dashboard artifact? :eyes:

maria_yu: Thanks for flagging. Which workloads specifically? small-chat is noisy, need the exact config you used.

alex_hernandez: small-chat, seq 512, batch target 32, sampling=true, kv_cache on. I attached the harness run id in the console: run/2026-03-10-11-22. The spike shows up around step 1200.

kevin: I'll kick off a repeat now with sampling=false and sampling=true to compare. Giving it a few minutes.

jin_park: Quick thought — did the batching window default change in the rollout? There was a PR that adjusted the batching latency cap to 6ms from 4ms. That could increase TTFT for small requests. @maria_yu any recall?

maria_yu: Yes, that was PR #4127 (adaptive-window tweak). It should only affect micro-batching when requests are sparse, but maybe interaction with sampling is exposing it.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout rtx-v2 completed at 2026-03-09T22:40Z on cluster-east-1.

kevin: Results: sampling=false p95 TTFT = 72ms, sampling=true p95 TTFT = 86ms. Baseline before the change was ~73ms. Looks like sampling adds a tail for some traces. Full logs: https://console/redwood/runs/run-2026-03-10-11-45

alex_hernandez: Cool thanks. Can we profile a single slow trace? If it's batching window hold then we should see more wait time in the scheduler.

taylor: I can pull a p95 trace and annotate. If it's scheduler wait, the span "batch_wait_ms" should be elevated. I'll post an example.

maria_yu: Also let's double-check how TTFT is defined in the dashboard. We capture TTFT as time-to-first-token from request start to first token emitted by runtime. But some dashboards were showing time-to-first-byte (including network) earlier — possible mismatch. We should verify the dashboard source.

jin_park: Good call. In Grafana the panel uses field `response.first_token_latency_ms` from metrics-v2. The code that emits that field was touched in the same PR. Worth validating the instrumentation too.

kevin: I ran a microprofile on the same run; here's the relevant diff:```json
{
  "batch_wait_ms": 9.3,
  "kernel_exec_ms": 1.8,
  "kv_lookup_ms": 0.7,
  "sampling_overhead_ms": 4.2
}
```Looks like sampling_overhead is non-trivial for small requests.

alex_hernandez: That matches my suspicion. Two asks: (1) can we add an ephemeral smoke alert that triggers if sampling=true increases p95 TTFT by >10% from baseline for seq<=512? (2) Can we file a quick perf PR to gate sampling overhead when batch size < 8?

maria_yu: For (1) I can add a one-off alert rule in the perf-alerting dashboard with scope filter sampling=true and seq<=512. For (2) I'll open a draft PR to short-circuit sampling path for tiny batches.

taylor: Draft alert rule:```
expr: increase(response.first_token_latency_ms{sampling="true",seq="<=512"}[10m]) > 0.10 * baseline_ttft
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: warning
```I'll post it to the perf-alerting board and link in the PR.

sre-bot: perf-bot: benchmark job queued: bench/small-chat/2026-03-10-12-05, ETA ~8m.

kevin: Bench finishes — new numbers pushed to dashboards. I also uploaded the raw traces to the artifacts bucket: s3://redwood-artifacts/perf/2026-03-10/small-chat/.

alex_hernandez: Thanks team. Last thing — can we update the metric doc snippet about TTFT to explicitly call out sampling overhead and how we measure it? I can draft a one-paragraph blurb.

maria_yu: Please do. Put the blurb in the shared docs under eng-runtime/perf-metrics.md and ping me for a quick review.

taylor: Added an annotation to the panel and a short note in the dashboard description.

maria_yu: Follow-up: I pushed a tiny rollback to revert the adaptive-window default to 4ms in prod for now; monitoring will show impact over the next hour. Keeping the sampling path active for testing.

alex_hernandez: Noted. Will re-run the smoke harness in ~30m and post final numbers. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
